learning.why: The teacher repeatedly connected the fraction to counting equal parts of the whole bar and used the 'one of three equal groups' phrase, which landed.
Didi showed that even if only 2 eaten, the whole was cut in 5, not 3 parts left, so I now know bottom is total.

end.summary:
Recognised halves, thirds, and quarters in equal parts across 5 attempts, with 4 unaided correct.
Initially described a fraction using shaded versus unshaded parts, then corrected this to parts out of the whole after prompting.
Identified 2/5 when two of five equal parts were eaten and explained why the denominator stayed five.
Identified unequal parts as not showing quarters and connected 2/4 with half.
Needed further support to apply one-third to nine drumsticks; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised recognising equal shares and naming halves, thirds, and quarters with Nisha. Nisha explained that the denominator tells the total number of equal parts and corrected the earlier mix-up between shaded and unshaded parts and the whole. They also identified 2/5 and saw that 2/4 is half. At home, practise sharing 6 or 9 small objects into three equal groups and ask how many objects are in one-third.
